overview.text: Stephen Curry, born Wardell Stephen Curry II, is an American professional basketball guard for the Golden State Warriors. After starring at Davidson College, where he led the Wildcats to the 2008 NCAA tournament Elite Eight, he was selected seventh overall by Golden State in 2009. Curry is especially known for his three-point shooting: in 2015–16, he made an NBA-record 402 three-pointers and became the league’s first unanimous Most Valuable Player. His long-range accuracy and willingness to shoot from far beyond the basket helped change how the game is played, making him one of modern basketball’s defining players.

key_facts.text: His full name is Wardell Stephen Curry II; he was born in Akron, Ohio, on March 14, 1988.
At Davidson, he led the Wildcats to the 2008 NCAA tournament Elite Eight and was named the Midwest Regional’s Most Outstanding Player.
The Golden State Warriors selected Curry seventh overall in the 2009 NBA Draft.
In 2015–16, Curry made 402 three-pointers, then an NBA single-season record, and became the NBA’s first unanimous MVP.
On December 14, 2021, he broke the NBA record for career three-pointers made.
